questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a roadmap add on top of a governance strategy?
options: A time-ordered sequence of the strategy's priorities that people can plan and budget against
A replacement business case that ignores the original strategy
A single fixed deadline for the entire program
A list of software vendors to purchase immediately
questions.explain: The strategy supplies the why and what; the roadmap supplies the when and in what order — a real sequence, not just a list.

questions.q: What are the three horizons this lesson recommends for a governance roadmap?
options: Now, Next, Later
Monday, Wednesday, Friday
Phase Alpha, Phase Beta, Phase Gamma
Daily, Weekly, Monthly
questions.explain: Now (funded, starting immediately), Next (planned, a few quarters out), and Later (directionally agreed, deliberately undetailed).

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a roadmap needs both quick wins and foundational investments?
options: An all-foundational roadmap loses patience before showing value, and an all-quick-win roadmap never builds the needed capability
Quick wins are always more expensive than foundational work
Foundational investments are optional and can be skipped entirely
Executives are only interested in foundational work, never quick wins
questions.explain: The two serve different purposes — visible value early, and the underlying capability that later work depends on.

questions.q: What does the lesson say happens when a roadmap skips dependency mapping?
options: An initiative starts on schedule and then stalls because it silently depended on an earlier initiative finishing first
Nothing changes — dependency mapping has no real effect on timelines
The roadmap automatically becomes a strategy
All initiatives are canceled immediately
questions.explain: The lesson's catalog-rollout example: it depends on the metadata architecture being settled, and skipping that check causes mid-roadmap stalls.

questions.q: According to the lesson's chapter roadmap, what comes right after roadmapping?
options: Governance Architecture Documentation
A final certification exam
Migrating to a new cloud vendor
Hiring an external auditor
questions.explain: Lesson 24 covers documenting the architecture and strategy so they survive turnover and actually get used.
